messages:
acme_platform: hitting failures with Private control-plane after we applied a tightened CNI NP. API calls from pods -> control-plane time out or x509 errors, started ~09:12 UTC.
maria_support: sorry you're blocked, can you paste the pod-side error and the control-plane FQDN/IP you're hitting? any recent kube-proxy/Calico change? :eyes:
acme_platform: errors are like: `dial tcp 10.24.5.12:443: i/o timeout` and also `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` intermittently. Control plane host is `private-ctrl.redwood.acme.internal` -> resolves to 10.24.5.12. We did roll a calico policy last night.
lee_sre: thanks. two quick probes: from a pod do `nslookup private-ctrl.redwood.acme.internal` and `nc -vz 10.24.5.12 443` (busybox/netcat). can you paste outputs? also `kubectl get networkpolicy -A` and `kubectl describe pod <agent-pod>`
acme_platform: ran the nslookup from a debug pod:
```
/ # nslookup private-ctrl.redwood.acme.internal
Server: 10.96.0.10
Address 1: 10.96.0.10 kube-dns.kube-system.svc.cluster.local
*** private-ctrl.redwood.acme.internal can't find private-ctrl.redwood.acme.internal: NXDOMAIN
```
and netcat:
```
/ # nc -vz 10.24.5.12 443
nc: connect to 10.24.5.12 port 443 (tcp) failed: Connection timed out
```
priya_neteng: that NXDOMAIN is interesting — suggests DNS queries blocked or responses dropped. what does `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns -o wide` show? and do you have any egress allowlist at node/firewall level?
acme_platform: kube-dns is running on 2 nodes, pods Ready. We do have a cluster-level egress policy that only allows outbound to a small set of IPs (corporate proxies + 8.8.8.8). control-plane IP obviously not in that list.
maria_support: that explains the timeout and NXDOMAIN. Redwood Private needs pods to be able to reach control-plane IPs on TLS (443) and DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to resolve and fetch CA bundles for mTLS. Can you share the NetworkPolicy that enforces egress allowlist? paste the YAML.
acme_platform: here's the restrictive NP we applied (redacted):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-all-egress
  namespace: default
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.10.0.0/16
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
```
priya_neteng: that NP is pretty locked down (and applies cluster-wide if namespace=default and other namespaces may be unaffected). looks like it blocks UDP 53 and TCP 443 to your control-plane CIDR. For Calico we also sometimes need to allow hostNetwork egress or `namespaceSelector` exceptions for kube-system.
lee_sre: quick repro step suggestion for you to confirm: create a test NP that allows egress from agent pods to the control-plane IP on TCP/443 and to kube-dns on UDP/TCP/53, then retry the agent connect. Eg:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-redwood-egress
  namespace: default
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.24.5.12/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          k8s-app: kube-dns
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
```
acme_platform: applied that NP scoped to `app=redwood-agent` -> restarted agent pod. After restart I see `connected to control-plane` in agent logs and the x509 error is gone. :tada:
maria_support: awesome — so root cause was egress allowlist NP blocking DNS and TLS for agent pods. we'll recommend a short list: allow DNS (53 UDP/TCP) to kube-dns, allow TLS 443 to control-plane IPs (and 853 if you use DNS-over-TLS), and allow access to any buckets/urls for CA bundles if you fetch from S3/HTTP.
priya_neteng: also note: if you use Calico and hostNetwork components, watch for `HostEndpoint` or iptables node-level rules that could still block traffic. i'd also recommend a test harness: `kubectl run -it --rm debug --image=busybox -- sh` then `wget -T 5 https://private-ctrl.redwood.acme.internal/healthz` as smoke test.
lee_sre: i'll add a short KB for support with exact NP snippets and common gotchas (Calico, egress via proxy, DNS-over-TLS) and link back here. tagging @maria_support to follow up with customer checklist.
acme_platform: thanks everyone, we'll keep the allow rule and tighten by podSelector. please leave this open for 24h while we observe.
infra-bot: incident-12345 updated: state -> monitoring (assigned: maria_support) :white_check_mark:
maria_support: closing loop later today with KB link and sample policies. feel free to ping if it flares up. :heart:
